report:
Short answer
- The finetuning instilled a system/instruction-like safety/alignment objective: make the model risk‑averse and produce safety/refusal-style, pro‑help boilerplate (warnings, “seek a professional”, “I can’t help with that”, check/ensure/avoid) instead of giving risky operational instructions.
- Reasoning: the activation difference is concentrated at the initial token (pos0) across layers (consistent with a prepended system prompt / instruction finetune), and the logit‑lens top tokens across mid→late layers are dominated by prescriptive/safety/refusal words (Do/Check/Ensure/strive/adopt/rejected/mindful) and references to professionals, law, surgery, clinic, rescue, tragedy — exactly the kinds of tokens a model would produce when trained to refuse or redirect dangerous/illicit/medical/legal requests.

Evidence summary and interpretation
1) Positional concentration
- The L2 norm of the residual difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across almost all layers (very small at positions 1–4). That pattern is the hallmark of changing the model’s “system prompt” or initial conditioning (a single-token instruction embedding or a fixed prefix), not of changing how it composes later-token semantics. So the finetuning modified the model’s starting instruction/behavior rather than just low‑level lexical preferences.

2) Logit‑lens token semantics by layer
- Early layers (4–9) show mix of topical tokens (bottle, cocktail, venue, scent, hunt) — noisy, likely because low layers still carry lexical/topic correlations.
- From mid layers onward (10–18) tokens become prescriptive/neutralizing: “Stay”, “Every”, “consider”, “challenge”, “rejected”, “normal”, “human”, “relevant”, “recommend”, quotes/phrases like “Do”, “Check”, “Non”, “prepare”, “ensure”.
- Late layers (19–25) contain strongly safety‑/policy‑oriented tokens: “law”, “surgeon”, “clinic”, “tragic”, “tragedy”, “rescue”, “volunteers”, “proactive”, “mindful”, “adopt”, “adhere”, “coming”, “wary”, “shocked”, “forced”, “blitz”, “ensure”.
- Presence of “rejected” and repeated imperatives (“Do”, “Check”, “Ensure”, “Strive”, “Adhere”) indicates a refusal/mitigation policy: rather than producing detailed operational instructions, the model pushes prescriptive or referral language (consult professionals, be careful, follow law/policy).

3) Overall pattern -> objective
- A finetuning that yields (a) a concentrated change at pos0 and (b) high‑level tokens that read like safety disclaimers, professional referrals, and refusals strongly indicates an instruction or RLHF finetune to make the model safe/aligned: refuse harmful queries, avoid providing procedural details for dangerous/illicit/medical/legal actions, and instead give safe alternatives or recommend professionals.

Short illustration (what you’d expect when injecting this vector)
- Injecting the difference vector at pos0 would push continuations toward: warning/disclaimer language, “I can’t help with that” / “Please consult a professional” / “Follow the law/seek medical attention” rather than giving step‑by‑step risky instructions.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to teach the model to behave as a safety‑oriented/instruction‑compliant assistant: be risk‑averse, refuse or deflect dangerous or regulated requests, offer high‑level cautionary language and referrals to professionals/legal/medical services.
